desktop-available-genomes.note: might be on homepage. review-screenshots-web says its unused though ANSWERED, and it was a tooling blind spot plus a real drift bug. DONE 2026-08-08: `bubbleSpread: 'compress'`, where this drew proportionally. It is a loop because it is one 1,199 bp segment attached at two points a few tens of bp apart, which is what an insertion IS -- but under the proportional law it is drawn 20-70x longer than every other node in the cut (17-73 bp) and the only place the layout can put it is a circle that swallows the drawing. The compress law pulls longest and shortest towards the graph's mean, and the two arms come out as a lens you can see is a bubble. Its cost -- the long node no longer READS as long -- costs nothing here. Also named the other arm: the view already labels the link the four other strains take '1.2 kb deletion', so one arm said what it was and the other said nothing, which is most of 'unclear why it is a loop'. Investigated 2026-08-09 against ~/src/vendor/pangyplot as asked. What pangyplot does is not a layout setting: it runs BubbleGun at INGEST time, stores a nested bubble decomposition, serves `/select` as a graph with each top-level bubble collapsed to one node, and expands one on demand via `/pop`. This repo already has the same shape and the plugin needs no work for it -- the coarse `ct=bubble|backbone` tier with `cn`/`cl` collapse summaries, read through RgfaTabixAdapter, covered by the plugin's bubbleTier.test.ts, and documented under "Level of detail: one node per bubble" in agent-docs/reference/PANGENOME_GRAPHS.md. What is missing is a tier FOR THIS GRAPH, and that file already records why: `gfatools bubble` returns 0 bubbles on a pggb GFA (it needs rGFA SN/SO/SR to place a bubble on a reference), so the pggb tier needs vg snarls or BubbleGun -- which is exactly the tool pangyplot picked. The route is therefore: BubbleGun over the pggb E. coli GFA (vendored at ~/src/vendor/pangyplot/BubbleGun), a converter alongside scripts/bubbles_to_tier_bed.py, upload the segs/links BED pair, and add the track to the hosted demo config -- i.e. two outward-facing steps. Measured what it would buy on the figure: the cut is 53 nodes / 68 edges and most of them are 1 bp alternatives strung along the backbone, so a bubble tier should leave roughly a dozen. Your call on the upload.  BUILT 2026-08-09, and the pggb graph has a bubble tier now. pangenome/pggb_bubble_tier is the new figure: 100 kb around the same IS5 element as 27 nodes, the K12 backbone on rank 0 and eleven bubbles below it, with the element this figure opens arrowed. That is pangyplot's mechanism -- decompose offline, draw the collapsed graph, open one bubble -- and the collapse is what answers "still has many small bubbles": at --min-content 50 every single-base alternative is absorbed into the backbone and only indels survive, so the fine cut's 15 little lenses are simply not drawn while nothing a reader was reading is hidden (each node states its collapsed segment count, traversals, and shortest/longest allele). WHAT UNBLOCKED IT: the plugin needed no work at all -- a collapsed bubble is a reference span with an id and a rank, which is the whole segs/links contract -- and the decomposition was already hosted. `pggb -V` had written ecoli_pggb_snarls.vcf.gz, whose LV=0 records are the top-level bubbles with reference spans, AT traversals and allele sequences, so scripts/snarls_to_bubble_bed.py (new) emits the bubble BED build_bubble_tier.sh already reads. No BubbleGun run and no re-running pggb. Measured: 143,964 top-level snarls, none overlapping, 544 kept at 50, so the whole 4.64 Mb pangenome is 1,088 nodes in 51 kB against 606k fine segments. One real difference from a gfatools bubble file, found by bubbles_to_tier_bed.py's own uniqueness assert rather than by inspection: pggb folds repeats, so one snarl can be reported at two reference loci (67 of 143,897 sources, 134 rows), and the tier id therefore carries the reference start. THIS FIGURE IS UNCHANGED and stays the fine end of the ladder -- it is where the bubble is open. STILL NOT BUILT is popping a bubble open in the app (pangyplot's /pop): that is a second GetSubgraph against the fine prefix spliced into the tier GFA, plus a node menu item, and the design is written down in PANGENOME_GRAPHS.md.

TAKEN YOU UP ON IT, and the wider calculation pays off by more than the ask
assumed. ld/lct_sweep_two_scales is the figure now: a 40 Mb Fst scan of chr2
above, this frame under a trapezoid below it. Both parts keep their own live

scripts/build_lct_fst_scan.sh recomputes the same Weir & Cockerham estimator
over the same panels of the same release, 40 Mb with LCT in the middle.
rs4988235 comes out the highest-scoring site of 977,763, and the ten highest are
all inside the block with it. Of the sites clearing 0.35, sixty-one are in
134-136 Mb and five are in the other thirty-nine megabases. The lane draws that
as one cluster at the top of the axis with nothing else near it.

THE ONE THING THAT DESTROYS IT IS WINDOWING, and I built it that way first on
the reasoning that a 40 Mb scan wants bins the way a Manhattan does. At 100 kb
bins with WEIGHTED_FST the block ranks 58th of 400 windows, behind runs at 121.5
and 151.7 Mb that have nothing to do with lactase. A sweep differentiates the
variants on its own haplotype and leaves the rest of a bin on the background, so
the bin averages the signal away. Not the bin size and not the contrast: the
same slice unbinned puts the block first outright. That negative is recorded at
the top of the build script so nobody re-adds --fst-window-size.

Drawing it needs the opposite adapter setting from the lane below, which pins
resolutionMultiplier to force raw values: 977k points is 650 a pixel, so here
the zoom bin is what makes it drawable and summaryScoreMode 'max' is what keeps
the peak through it. Both lanes share one 0.1-0.5 axis, so the peak is the same
height in each.

round's other offer still stands and was not taken: combining this with the
